nodes.label: Geometric constructions
nodes.title: Creating exact geometric figures using formal procedures with compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Applying geometric constructions to real-life contexts
nodes.title: Using constructions to solve practical layout, design, and measurement problems (e.g., bisecting spaces, setting right angles, laying out circles).

nodes.label: Drawing a circle of given radius
nodes.title: Using a compass set to a specified length to draw a circle centered at a point.

nodes.label: Use of a straightedge (unmarked ruler)
nodes.title: Drawing straight lines and extending segments without measurement.

nodes.label: Use of a compass
nodes.title: Transferring lengths and drawing arcs/circles for constructions.

nodes.label: Use of a ruler (measuring length)
nodes.title: Measuring and marking lengths accurately on diagrams.

nodes.label: Use of a protractor (measuring angles)
nodes.title: Measuring and marking angles to a required degree measure.

nodes.label: Use of a set square
nodes.title: Drawing perpendicular and specific-angle lines (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°) accurately.

nodes.label: Perpendicular bisector construction
nodes.title: Constructing the line that is perpendicular to a segment and passes through its midpoint using a compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Angle bisector construction
nodes.title: Constructing a ray that divides a given angle into two equal angles with compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Constructing a perpendicular line through a given point
nodes.title: Creating a line perpendicular to a given line either through a point on the line or a point not on the line.

nodes.label: Constructing a parallel line through a given point
nodes.title: Using compass-and-straightedge methods (e.g., corresponding angles) to draw a line parallel to a given line through a specified point.

nodes.label: Dynamic geometry software for constructions
nodes.title: Using digital tools (e.g., GeoGebra) to create, explore, and verify geometric constructions dynamically.

nodes.label: Precision and accuracy in geometric drawings
nodes.title: Applying correct instrument techniques to reduce error and produce exact constructions.

nodes.label: Cartesian coordinate plane
nodes.title: The two-dimensional plane defined by perpendicular x- and y-axes used to locate points with ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Ordered pairs (x, y)
nodes.title: A pair of numbers that uniquely identifies a point on the coordinate plane.

nodes.label: Plotting points on the coordinate plane
nodes.title: Placing points at given coordinates relative to the axes and origin.

nodes.label: Linear relationships in real-world contexts
nodes.title: Modeling real-life situations where one quantity changes at a constant rate with respect to another.

nodes.label: Tabular representation of linear relationships
nodes.title: Using value tables (x and corresponding y) to represent and analyze linear patterns.

nodes.label: Graphical representation of linear relationships
nodes.title: Plotting points and drawing straight lines to model linear functions on the coordinate plane.

nodes.label: Slope of a line
nodes.title: A measure of steepness of a line, often computed as rise over run (Δy/Δx).

nodes.label: Rate of change
nodes.title: Change in the dependent variable per unit change in the independent variable; constant for linear relationships.

nodes.label: Equivalence of slope and rate of change
nodes.title: Recognizing that the slope of a linear graph equals the contextual rate at which one quantity changes relative to another.

nodes.label: Y-intercept (start value)
nodes.title: The value of the dependent variable when the independent variable is zero; the initial value in context.

nodes.label: Interpreting intercepts in context
nodes.title: Explaining the meaning of the start value and other intercepts with respect to a real-world situation.

nodes.label: Comparing linear relationships
nodes.title: Analyzing and contrasting lines using slope (rate of change) and intercepts (start values).

nodes.label: Independent and dependent variables in linear models
nodes.title: Identifying which quantity is controlled (x) and which responds (y) in a linear relationship.

nodes.label: Point of intersection of two lines
nodes.title: The coordinate pair that satisfies both linear relationships simultaneously.

nodes.label: Interpreting intersection in context (break-even point)
nodes.title: Understanding the practical significance of where two linear models yield the same value.

nodes.label: Solving systems of linear equations by graphing
nodes.title: Finding the solution to two linear relationships by locating their point of intersection on a graph.

nodes.label: Graphical strategies for solving linear problems
nodes.title: Using graphs to estimate or determine solutions to linear equations and systems from context.

nodes.label: Numeric (tabular) strategies for solving linear problems
nodes.title: Using tables of values to compute, compare, and find solutions to linear relationships.

nodes.label: Mental strategies and estimation for linear problems
nodes.title: Estimating slopes, intercepts, and intersections to check reasonableness of solutions in context.

nodes.label: Right-angled triangles
nodes.title: Triangles with one 90° angle; sides include two legs and the hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Hypotenuse in a right triangle
nodes.title: The side opposite the right angle; the longest side of a right triangle.

nodes.label: Opposite and adjacent sides relative to an angle
nodes.title: Naming the leg opposite or adjacent to a given acute angle in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Pythagorean Theorem
nodes.title: In a right triangle, a^2 + b^2 = c^2, relating legs to the hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Applying the Pythagorean Theorem to heights and distances
nodes.title: Solving contextual right-triangle problems (e.g., ladders, buildings, line-of-sight) using a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios in right triangles
nodes.title: Definition of sine, cosine, and tangent as ratios of side lengths in a right triangle.

nodes.label: SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic
nodes.title: Mnemonic for remembering sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.

nodes.label: Selecting appropriate trigonometric ratio
nodes.title: Choosing sine, cosine, or tangent based on which sides are known and which are unknown.

nodes.label: Finding unknown side lengths using trigonometric ratios
nodes.title: Computing a missing leg or hypotenuse from an angle and a side using sine, cosine, or tangent.

nodes.label: Finding unknown angles using inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Using arcsin, arccos, or arctan to determine an angle from side-length ratios.

nodes.label: Angles of elevation and depression
nodes.title: Angles measured above or below a horizontal line used in real-world right-triangle models.

nodes.label: Modeling real-world situations with right triangles
nodes.title: Translating contextual scenarios (heights, distances, ramps, sightlines) into right-triangle diagrams.

nodes.label: Solving right triangles
nodes.title: Determining all unknown sides and angles using Pythagoras, trigonometric ratios, and inverse trig functions.

nodes.label: Transformation geometry
nodes.title: Study of geometric transformations and their properties in the plane.

nodes.label: Translation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: Shifts every point of a figure by the same vector, preserving distances and orientation.

nodes.label: Rotation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: Turns a figure about a fixed center by a given angle, preserving distances and angles.

nodes.label: Axial symmetry (line reflection)
nodes.title: Reflection of a figure across a line (axis), producing a mirror image.

nodes.label: Central symmetry (point reflection)
nodes.title: A half-turn (180-degree rotation) about a point that maps each point to its opposite relative to the center.

nodes.label: Locating axes of symmetry in simple shapes
nodes.title: Identifying lines that divide a shape into two mirror-image halves.

nodes.label: Image under a transformation
nodes.title: The resulting point or figure after applying a specified geometric transformation.

nodes.label: Enlargement (dilation)
nodes.title: A similarity transformation that scales a figure from a center by a scale factor k > 0.

nodes.label: Centre of enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which distances are scaled along rays during an enlargement.

nodes.label: Scale factor of enlargement
nodes.title: The multiplicative factor k that scales all distances from the center in an enlargement.

nodes.label: Reduction (0 < k < 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor between 0 and 1 that produces a smaller similar image.

nodes.label: Magnification (k > 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor greater than 1 that produces a larger similar image.

nodes.label: Rational scale factor (k ∈ Q)
nodes.title: Using rational numbers as scale factors in enlargements, including fractional scaling.

nodes.label: Area scaling under enlargement
nodes.title: Under an enlargement with scale factor k, the area of a figure scales by k^2.

nodes.label: Recognising images under transformations
nodes.title: Identifying the result of applying translations, rotations, axial symmetry, or central symmetry to points and shapes.

nodes.label: Solving problems involving enlargements
nodes.title: Applying center and scale factor to find images/preimages, lengths, and areas in enlargement contexts.

nodes.label: Rigid motions (isometries)
nodes.title: Transformations that preserve distances and angles, including translations, rotations, and reflections.

nodes.label: Synthetic geometry
nodes.title: Study of geometry using axioms, theorems, and constructions without coordinates or algebra.

nodes.label: Compass-and-straightedge constructions (16–21)
nodes.title: Perform a specified set of classical geometric constructions labeled 16–21 in the syllabus.

nodes.label: Compass-and-straightedge construction 22
nodes.title: Execute the syllabus' construction number 22 using a compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Theorem (geometric)
nodes.title: A mathematical statement that can be proven from axioms and previously established results.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.title: A logically coherent argument establishing the truth of a theorem.

nodes.label: Axiom
nodes.title: A foundational assumption accepted without proof, used to derive theorems.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A proposition that follows readily from a theorem with little or no additional proof.

nodes.label: Converse of a statement
nodes.title: The statement formed by reversing the hypothesis and conclusion of an implication.

nodes.label: Logical implication (implies)
nodes.title: A relationship A → B meaning if A is true, then B must also be true.

nodes.label: Logical equivalence
nodes.title: Two statements that always have the same truth value; each implies the other.

nodes.label: Biconditional (if and only if)
nodes.title: The statement A iff B, asserting both A → B and B → A.

nodes.label: Proof by contradiction
nodes.title: An indirect proof technique that assumes the negation of the desired result and derives a contradiction.

nodes.label: Investigating geometric theorems through problem solving
nodes.title: Exploring, testing, and applying named theorems (e.g., 7, 8, 11–13, 16–18, 20–21) to solve geometric problems.

nodes.label: Corollary 6 (application in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: Use of a specified corollary labeled 6 in the syllabus to deduce further results and solve problems.

nodes.label: Theorem 11 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem concerning ratios in geometric figures, supporting later results.

nodes.label: Theorem 12 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem on ratios in geometry, forming part of the foundation for subsequent proofs.

nodes.label: Theorem 13 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem dealing with ratios in geometric contexts that underpins further results.

nodes.label: Geometric ratios and proportionality
nodes.title: Reasoning with ratios in geometric figures (e.g., segment lengths) to derive relationships and proofs.

nodes.label: Foundation for the Pythagorean theorem
nodes.title: Results and ratio arguments that prepare for the formal proof of the Pythagorean theorem.

nodes.label: Deductive reasoning in geometry
nodes.title: Deriving conclusions from axioms and theorems using logically valid steps.

nodes.label: Parallel lines criterion via slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.

nodes.label: Perpendicular lines criterion via slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes are negative reciprocals (m1 · m2 = -1).

nodes.label: Linear equation in general form (ax + by + c = 0)
nodes.title: Represents a straight line in the plane; coefficients determine slope and intercepts.

nodes.label: Angle between two lines using slopes
nodes.title: For slopes m1 and m2, tan(θ) = |(m1 − m2)/(1 + m1·m2)| gives the acute angle between lines.

nodes.label: Perpendicular distance from a point to a line
nodes.title: Distance from (x0, y0) to Ax + By + C = 0 is |Ax0 + By0 + C| / √(A2 + B2).

nodes.label: Internal division of a line segment (section formula)
nodes.title: Point dividing segment A(x1,y1) and B(x2,y2) internally in ratio m:n has coordinates ((mx2 + nx1)/(m+n), (my2 + ny1)/(m+n)).

nodes.label: Area of a triangle in the coordinate plane
nodes.title: Area with vertices (x1,y1),(x2,y2),(x3,y3) is 1/2 |x1(y2−y3) + x2(y3−y1) + x3(y1−y2)| (shoelace method).

nodes.label: Center-radius form of a circle equation
nodes.title: (x − h)2 + (y − k)2 = r2 represents all points at distance r from center (h, k).

nodes.label: General form of a circle equation
nodes.title: x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a circle with center (−g, −f) and radius r = √(g2 + f2 − c).

nodes.label: Equation of a circle centered at the origin
nodes.title: x2 + y2 = r2 describes a circle with center (0, 0) and radius r.

nodes.label: Line–circle intersection (center at origin)
nodes.title: Solving a line with x2 + y2 = r2 to find intersection points; includes cases of secant, tangent, or no intersection.

nodes.label: Line–circle intersection (general)
nodes.title: Solving simultaneous equations of a line and a circle to determine intersection points and tangency conditions.

nodes.label: Pythagorean theorem (2D)
nodes.title: In a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the legs equals the square of the hypotenuse (a^2 + b^2 = c^2); used to solve planar problems.

nodes.label: Area of a triangle using trigonometry
nodes.title: Compute area with A = (1/2)ab sin C when two sides and the included angle are known.

nodes.label: Sine rule (Law of sines)
nodes.title: Relates sides and angles in any triangle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C; used to find unknown sides/angles.

nodes.label: Cosine rule (Law of cosines)
nodes.title: Generalizes Pythagoras: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 − 2ab cos C (and cyclic forms) to find sides/angles in any triangle.

nodes.label: Definition of sin θ for all real θ
nodes.title: Extends sine to all real angles (e.g., via the unit circle), allowing positive/negative values and periodicity.

nodes.label: Definition of cos θ for all real θ
nodes.title: Extends cosine to all real angles (e.g., via the unit circle) with even symmetry and period 2π.

nodes.label: Definition of tan θ
nodes.title: Defines tangent as tan θ = sin θ / cos θ with undefined values where cos θ = 0; period π.

nodes.label: Area of a sector of a circle
nodes.title: Area given by A = (1/2) r^2 θ (radians) or A = (θ/360) π r^2 (degrees).

nodes.label: Arc length of a circle
nodes.title: Arc length given by s = r θ (radians) or s = (θ/360) 2π r (degrees).

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios in surd form
nodes.title: Use exact radical values for sin, cos, tan of special angles (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°) instead of decimals.

nodes.label: 3D trigonometry problem solving
nodes.title: Apply trigonometric methods to three-dimensional contexts to find lengths, angles, and distances.

nodes.label: Graph of y = sin θ
nodes.title: Sine function graph with amplitude 1, period 2π, and key intercepts/maximum/minimum points.

nodes.label: Graph of y = cos θ
nodes.title: Cosine function graph with amplitude 1, period 2π, starting at maximum when θ = 0.

nodes.label: Graph of y = tan θ
nodes.title: Tangent function graph with period π and vertical asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2.

nodes.label: Graphing transformed sine functions a + b sin(cθ)
nodes.title: Plot sinusoidal graphs with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Graphing transformed cosine functions a + b cos(cθ)
nodes.title: Plot cosine graphs with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: General solutions of trigonometric equations
nodes.title: Find all solutions using periodicity, e.g., sin(nθ) = 0 implies θ = kπ/n for integers k.

nodes.label: Solving equations like cos(nθ) = 1/2
nodes.title: Determine principal solutions and express the infinite family of solutions using k ∈ Z.

nodes.label: Radian measure of angles
nodes.title: Measure angles via arc length: θ = s/r; convert between degrees and radians and use radians in formulas.

nodes.label: Derivation of core trigonometric identities
nodes.title: Prove identities such as Pythagorean, angle addition/subtraction, and double-angle formulas.

nodes.label: Application of trigonometric identities
nodes.title: Use identities to simplify expressions, transform formulas, and solve trigonometric equations.

nodes.label: Reduction (0<k<1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor 0<k<1 that produces a smaller, similar image; all linear dimensions are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Magnification (k>1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor k>1 that produces a larger, similar image; all linear dimensions are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Constructing an enlargement with given center and scale factor
nodes.title: A procedure using rays from the center through object points and proportional distances to draw the image at scale factor k.

nodes.label: Finding the centre of enlargement from object and image
nodes.title: A method to locate the center by joining pairs of corresponding points and intersecting the lines through them.

nodes.label: Relating linear and area scale factors
nodes.title: Understanding that linear measures scale by k while areas scale by k^2 in an enlargement.
